note: Majority: Civil Code (consolidated by the Legislative Assembly's Unidad de Actualización Normativa, the version WIPO Lex holds, July 2000), Article 37 as amended by Law No. 5476 of 21 December 1973: those who have turned 18 are of age; Article 38 makes a minor under 15 absolutely incapable of binding himself by contract, save as to marriage, and older minors' acts voidable, which the form doesn't hold. Service: Political Constitution, Article 12, read by eye in the Assembly's consolidated text WIPO Lex holds (its PDF's text layer is unreadable): the Army is proscribed as a permanent institution; military forces may be organised only by continental agreement or for national defence. No peacetime call-up, so none is held. Work: not held. The Children and Adolescents Code (Law No. 7739) sets the minimum working age, and what it says of child performers wasn't read: the Attorney General's legal database (pgrweb.go.cr/scij) answers with a Web Application Firewall block, the Ministry of Labour's site (mtss.go.cr) gives no page on it without its script menu, and the child welfare agency (pani.go.cr) sits behind a Cloudflare challenge, none of which was passed.

sources.title: WIPO Lex, Código Civil de Costa Rica (consolidated version of July 2000)
sources.said: ARTÍCULO 37.- Son mayores de edad las personas que han cumplido dieciocho años; y menores las que no han llegado a esa edad. (Así reformado por Ley No. 5476 del 21 de diciembre de 1973).

sources.title: WIPO Lex, Constitución Política de la República de Costa Rica (Assembly consolidated text), Article 12
sources.said: ARTÍCULO 12.- Se proscribe el Ejército como institución permanente. Para la vigilancia y conservación del orden público, habrá las fuerzas de policía necesarias.
